instructions: Questions from the 2025/2026 continuous assessment (CA) CBT. Every answer is explained after you submit.

questions.text: If the scalar product of two vectors is zero, the vectors are?
questions.explanation: $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B} = AB\cos\theta$. It is zero for non-zero vectors only when θ = 90°.

questions.text: The magnitude of the vector product of two parallel vectors is?
options: Equal to the product of their magnitudes
questions.explanation: $|\vec{A}\times\vec{B}| = AB\sin\theta$, and sin 0° = 0.

questions.text: Which of the following represents the result of the dot product of a vector with itself?
questions.explanation: $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{A} = A^2\cos 0° = A^2$.

questions.text: The cross product of two vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ results in a vector that is?
options: Perpendicular to the plane containing $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$
At an angle of 45° to both vectors
In the same direction as the scalar product
questions.explanation: The cross product is perpendicular to the plane that contains the two vectors.

questions.text: In classical mechanics, the state of motion or rest of an object is defined relative to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Whether an object is moving or at rest depends on the frame of reference chosen.

questions.text: The tendency of a stationary object to remain at rest unless acted upon by an external force is primarily described by?
questions.explanation: Newton's first law says an object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless a net external force acts.

questions.text: If an object is moving at a constant velocity, what can be concluded about the net force acting upon it?
options: The net force is equal to the object's mass
The net force is directed toward the center of motion
questions.explanation: Constant velocity means zero acceleration, so the net force is zero.

questions.text: When calculating the dot product of two perpendicular vectors, the resulting scalar value is?
questions.explanation: cos 90° = 0, so the dot product of perpendicular vectors is zero.

questions.text: A constant force of 1000 N acts on a mass $m_1$, producing an initial acceleration of 10 m/s². When an additional mass m is added to $m_1$, the same force produces a new acceleration that is two-thirds of the initial value. Calculate the value of $m_1$ and the new acceleration.
questions.explanation: $m_1 = F/a = 1000/10 = 100$ kg. The new acceleration is $\frac{2}{3} \times 10 = 6.67$ m/s².

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the sign conventions for distance and displacement?
options: Distance can be negative, while displacement is always positive
Distance is always positive or zero, while displacement can be positive, negative, or zero
Both distance and displacement must always be positive
Displacement is always positive, while distance can be zero
questions.explanation: Distance is a length of path, so it is never negative. Displacement has direction, so it can be positive, negative or zero.

questions.text: What is the fundamental difference between speed and velocity?
options: Speed is a vector quantity, while velocity is a scalar quantity
Velocity includes direction, while speed only represents magnitude
Speed is measured in m/s, while velocity is measured in m/s²
There is no difference between the two in classical mechanics
questions.explanation: Velocity is speed with direction.

questions.text: A unit vector is specifically defined as a vector having?
options: The same direction as the x-axis only
A magnitude equal to the mass of the object
questions.explanation: A unit vector has magnitude 1.

questions.text: In vector algebra, the unit vector is primarily used to?
options: Change the magnitude of a vector
Represent the scalar component of a motion
Specify the direction of a vector quantity
Calculate the area of a parallelogram
questions.explanation: A unit vector shows direction only.

questions.text: An object moves from a starting point to a destination 50 meters away and then returns to the starting point. What is the final displacement?
questions.explanation: The object ends where it started, so displacement is zero. The distance is 100 m.

questions.text: What is the value of the relative velocity of an object when measured with respect to itself?
questions.explanation: The velocity of an object relative to itself is $v - v = 0$.

questions.text: Based on the rules of unit vector cross products, which of the following identities is NOT correct?
questions.explanation: $\hat{j}\times\hat{i} = -\hat{k}$, so writing it as $\hat{k}$ is wrong.

questions.text: Given the vector $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}$, what is its magnitude?
If $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}$ and $\vec{B} = \hat{i} + \hat{j}$, find $\vec{A} - \vec{B}$.
Consider three vectors A, B, and C. The operation A - B - C represents?
options: The scalar sum of the vectors
The vector subtraction of B and C from A
The cross product of the three vectors
questions.explanation: Subtracting B and C from A gives A − B − C.

questions.text: Which of the following is the result of the dot product $\hat{i}\cdot\hat{i}$?
questions.explanation: $\hat{i}\cdot\hat{i} = 1 \times 1 \times \cos 0° = 1$.

questions.text: If the cross product of two non-zero vectors A and B results in a null vector, the vectors must be?
questions.explanation: A null cross product of non-zero vectors means sin θ = 0, so they are parallel.

questions.text: Given the vector equations $\vec{A} - \vec{B} = 2\vec{C}$ and $\vec{A} + \vec{B} = 4\vec{C}$, where $\vec{C} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}$, what is the vector $\vec{B}$?
questions.explanation: Subtract the first equation from the second: $2\vec{B} = 2\vec{C}$, so $\vec{B} = \vec{C} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}$.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of an inertial reference frame?
options: It is accelerating and Newton’s laws do not hold true
It is not accelerating and Newton’s laws do not hold true
It is accelerating and Newton’s laws hold true
It is not accelerating and Newton’s laws hold true
questions.explanation: An inertial frame does not accelerate, and Newton's laws hold in it.

questions.text: What is the value of the cross product $\hat{j}\times\hat{i}$?
questions.explanation: $\hat{i}\times\hat{j} = \hat{k}$, and reversing the order changes the sign.

questions.text: If vector $\vec{P} = 4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$, what is the magnitude of the unit vector acting in the direction of $\vec{P}$?
questions.explanation: Every unit vector has magnitude 1.

questions.text: The operation $\hat{k}\cdot(\hat{i}\times\hat{j})$ results in which of the following values?
questions.explanation: $\hat{i}\times\hat{j} = \hat{k}$ and $\hat{k}\cdot\hat{k} = 1$.

questions.text: If the dot product of two vectors is equal to the product of their magnitudes, the angle between them is?
questions.explanation: AB cos θ = AB means cos θ = 1, so θ = 0°.

questions.text: What are the dimensions of density?
questions.explanation: Density = mass/volume, so its dimensions are ML⁻³.

questions.text: A footballer kicks a ball with an initial velocity of 20 m/s at an angle of 45° to the horizontal. What is the horizontal range? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: $R = \frac{u^2\sin 2\theta}{g} = \frac{400 \times \sin 90°}{10} = 40$ m.

questions.text: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity of 20 m/s. Using g = 9.8 m/s², find the maximum height reached by the ball.
Which of the following statements is true regarding the distance and displacement of a moving body?
options: Distance is always equal to displacement
Displacement can be zero even if distance is non-zero
questions.explanation: A round trip covers distance but has zero displacement.

questions.text: If an object is moving at a constant speed in a straight line, its acceleration is?
questions.explanation: Constant speed in a straight line is constant velocity, so acceleration is zero.

questions.text: Which of the following is the unit of a unit vector?
questions.explanation: A unit vector is a vector divided by its own magnitude, so the units cancel.

questions.text: The horizontal component of a projectile's velocity, ignoring air resistance, is?
questions.explanation: With no air resistance no horizontal force acts, so the horizontal velocity stays constant.

questions.text: Which two events occur at the same location in the diagram?
questions.explanation: Events A and C are both at position P₁ (at different times). A and B happen at the same time but at different positions.
questions.imageAlt: Space-time diagram with position (x, y, z) on the vertical axis and time on the other. Event A is at position P1 and time t1. Event B is at position P2 and time t1. Event C is at position P1 and time t2.

questions.text: What is the dimension of wavelength?
questions.explanation: Wavelength is a length, so its dimension is L.

questions.text: Which of the following is the definition of space-time?
options: A combination of space and time into a single four-dimensional continuum
The concept that time is absolute
The separation of time from space
The fundamental unit of classical mechanics
questions.explanation: Space-time joins three space dimensions and time into one four-dimensional continuum.

questions.text: Given the vectors $\vec{A} = 4\hat{i} - 1.5\hat{j}$, $\vec{B} = -1.2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$ and $\vec{C} = -2.8\hat{j}$, calculate $\vec{A} - \vec{B} - \vec{C}$.

Two bodies, A and B, each have a mass of 10 kg. Body A has an initial velocity of $-25\hat{i} - 30\hat{j}$ and body B has an initial velocity of $20\hat{i} + 10\hat{j}$. If the final velocity of body A is $-15\hat{i} + 25\hat{j}$ after an interaction, and the system is isolated, what is the final velocity of body B?
questions.explanation: Masses are equal, so $\vec{v}_B = \vec{u}_A + \vec{u}_B - \vec{v}_A = (-5\hat{i} - 20\hat{j}) - (-15\hat{i} + 25\hat{j}) = 10\hat{i} - 45\hat{j}$.

questions.text: In the absence of external forces, the total momentum of a system of interacting bodies remains?
questions.explanation: With no external force, total momentum is conserved.

questions.text: If the mass of an object is doubled while the net force acting on it remains constant, the acceleration will?
questions.explanation: a = F/m, so doubling m halves a.

questions.text: Which of the following vector operations is used to determine the work done by a force over a displacement?
questions.explanation: Work is $\vec{F}\cdot\vec{d}$, a scalar product.

questions.text: A vector is said to be a null vector if?
options: Its direction is fixed at the origin
It is parallel to the x-axis
It has a magnitude of unity
questions.explanation: A null vector has zero magnitude.

questions.text: Given the vectors $\vec{A} = 4\hat{i} - 1.5\hat{j}$, $\vec{B} = -1.2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$ and $\vec{C} = -2.8\hat{j}$, calculate $\vec{A} - \vec{B} + \vec{C}$.
Consider the vector equations $\vec{A} - \vec{B} = 2\vec{C}$ and $\vec{A} + \vec{B} = 4\vec{C}$. If $\vec{C} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}$, determine the vector $\vec{A}$.
questions.explanation: Add the equations: $2\vec{A} = 6\vec{C}$, so $\vec{A} = 3\vec{C} = 9\hat{i} + 12\hat{j}$.

questions.text: If a system of vectors satisfies the condition A + B = 4C, the resultant vector of A and B is?
questions.explanation: The resultant is 4 times C, so it is parallel to C.

questions.text: In the vector operation A - B, the direction of the resultant vector is determined by?
options: Adding the magnitude of B to A
Adding the negative of vector B to vector A
Multiplying the components of A and B
The dot product of A and B
questions.explanation: A − B means A + (−B).

questions.text: If vector $\vec{C} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}$, what is the unit vector in the direction of $\vec{C}$?
questions.explanation: The magnitude of C is $\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5$, so the unit vector is C divided by 5.

questions.text: A body of mass 16 kg moving at 8 m/s collides with a body of mass 7 kg moving at 4 m/s in the same direction. If the collision is perfectly inelastic, find their common velocity after the collision.

If $\vec{A} = 3\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$, $\vec{B} = -\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{C} = 2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$, find the scalar triple product $\vec{A}\cdot(\vec{B}\times\vec{C})$.
questions.explanation: $\vec{B}\times\vec{C} = -8\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}$. Then $\vec{A}\cdot(\vec{B}\times\vec{C}) = -24 + 15 - 12 = -21$.

questions.text: Body A moves at 8 m/s North and Body B moves at 6 m/s South. What is the velocity of A with respect to B?
questions.explanation: Take north as positive: 8 − (−6) = 14 m/s north.

questions.text: A body of mass 16 kg moving at 8 m/s collides with a body of mass 7 kg moving at 4 m/s in the same direction. If the collision is perfectly inelastic, calculate the kinetic energy lost during the impact (to the nearest joule where needed).
questions.explanation: Initial KE = 512 + 56 = 568 J. Common velocity = 156/23 m/s, so final KE = ½ × 23 × (156/23)² = 529 J. Lost: about 39 J.

questions.text: Which of the following defines an inelastic collision?
options: Momentum is conserved, but kinetic energy is not
Kinetic energy is conserved, but momentum is not
Both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved
Neither momentum nor kinetic energy is conserved
questions.explanation: In an inelastic collision momentum is conserved but some kinetic energy is lost.

questions.text: In the vector calculation $\vec{A}\cdot(\vec{B}\times\vec{C})$, if the result is zero, it implies that the three vectors are?
questions.explanation: The scalar triple product is the volume of the box formed by the vectors. Zero volume means they lie in one plane.

questions.text: Three forces of 20 N, 40 N and 60 N act on a body of mass 250 g at angles of 0°, 30° and 60° respectively. Find the resulting force vector acting on the body.
Given the vectors $\vec{D}_1 = 3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$ and $\vec{D}_2 = -5\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}$, calculate $2\vec{D}_1\cdot 4\vec{D}_2$.

A body of mass 200 g moves in a straight line in the positive-x direction at 25 m/s. It hits a wall and rebounds in the negative-x direction at 35 m/s. If the interaction lasts 2 seconds, find the magnitude of the average force exerted.
questions.explanation: $F = \frac{m\Delta v}{t} = \frac{0.2 \times (35 + 25)}{2} = 6$ N.

questions.text: A body of mass 200 g moves in a straight line in the positive-x direction at 25 m/s. It hits a wall and rebounds in the negative-x direction at 35 m/s. If the interaction lasts 1 second, find the magnitude of the average force exerted.
questions.explanation: $F = \frac{m\Delta v}{t} = \frac{0.2 \times (35 + 25)}{1} = 12$ N.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of impulse?
questions.explanation: Impulse = force × time, so its unit is the newton-second.

questions.text: In a collision where two bodies stick together after impact, which of the following is conserved?
options: Both linear momentum and kinetic energy
questions.explanation: Sticking together is a perfectly inelastic collision: momentum is conserved, kinetic energy is not.

questions.text: If a vector is multiplied by a negative scalar other than −1, the resulting vector will have?
options: The opposite direction and same magnitude
The opposite direction and changed magnitude
questions.explanation: A negative scalar reverses the direction, and any size other than 1 changes the magnitude.

questions.text: A goalkeeper throws a ball from ground level with an initial speed of 20 m/s at an angle of 45°. How long will it take for the ball to reach the ground? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: $T = \frac{2u\sin\theta}{g} = \frac{2 \times 20 \times \sin 45°}{10} = 2.8$ s.

questions.text: If body A moves with an acceleration of 3 m/s² along the x-axis, and body B moves with an acceleration of 1 m/s² in the same direction, find the acceleration of A relative to B.
questions.explanation: Relative acceleration = 3 − 1 = 2 m/s².

questions.text: Which of the following represents the dimensional formula for Force?
questions.explanation: F = ma, so its dimensions are M × LT⁻² = MLT⁻².

questions.text: If body P is moving at 15 m/s and body Q is moving at 20 m/s in the same direction, what is the velocity of Q relative to P?
questions.explanation: Velocity of Q relative to P = 20 − 15 = 5 m/s.

questions.text: Body A moves at 40 m/s East and Body B moves at 30 m/s West. Find the velocity of A with respect to B?
questions.explanation: Take east as positive: 40 − (−30) = 70 m/s east.

questions.text: The position of a particle is given by $x = 2t^2 + 4$. Find the acceleration of the particle when t = 3 seconds.
questions.explanation: v = dx/dt = 4t and a = dv/dt = 4 m/s², which is constant.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding physical quantities and their relationships is incorrect?
options: Force is the rate of change of momentum
Acceleration is the rate of change of momentum
Impulse is the change in momentum
Power is the rate of doing work
questions.explanation: The rate of change of momentum is force. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.

questions.text: A 15 kg mass moves with a velocity of 8 m/s East and collides with a 5 kg mass moving in the opposite direction at 4 m/s. If the collision is perfectly inelastic, calculate the value of the kinetic energy lost?
questions.explanation: Common velocity = (15×8 − 5×4)/20 = 5 m/s. KE: 480 + 40 = 520 J before, ½ × 20 × 25 = 250 J after. Lost: 270 J.

questions.text: Given the vectors $\vec{D}_1 = 3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$ and $\vec{D}_2 = 5\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}$, find $\vec{D}_1\times 4\vec{D}_2$.
questions.explanation: $\vec{D}_1\times\vec{D}_2 = -10\hat{i} + 23\hat{j} + 19\hat{k}$. Multiply by 4 to get $-40\hat{i} + 92\hat{j} + 76\hat{k}$.

questions.text: If a collision is described as perfectly inelastic, it implies that?
options: The two bodies bounce off each other with no energy loss
The two bodies stick together and move with a common velocity
Kinetic energy is conserved but momentum is lost
The final velocity of the system is always zero
questions.explanation: In a perfectly inelastic collision the bodies stick together and share one velocity.

questions.text: A body of mass 16 kg travelling at 8 m/s collides perfectly inelastically with a mass of 7 kg travelling in the same direction at 4 m/s. Calculate the magnitude of the impulse on the 16 kg mass.
questions.explanation: Common velocity is 6.78 m/s. Impulse = 16 × (6.78 − 8) = −19.5, so its magnitude is 19.5 Ns.

questions.text: If a force is applied to a body for a very short period of time, the product of the force and the time interval is defined as?
questions.explanation: Impulse = force × time.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT usually a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Electric current has a direction of flow but does not add like a vector, so it is a scalar.

questions.text: The unit of pressure is?
questions.explanation: Pressure is measured in pascals (N/m²).

questions.text: A vehicle changes speed from 25 km/h to 90 km/h in 5.6 seconds. Find the acceleration.
The use of relative motion includes the following except?
options: Predicting the coming of a new moon
questions.explanation: Eclipses and new moons are predicted from the relative motion of the earth, moon and sun.

questions.text: Which of the following consists wholly of fundamental quantities?
options: Length, area, current, time, temperature, mass
Length, velocity, current, time, temperature, mass
Length, area, current, volume, temperature, mass
questions.explanation: Length, current, time, temperature and mass are all fundamental. Area, volume and velocity are derived.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes a particle?
questions.explanation: A particle is an idealised body with mass but no size.

questions.text: A particle has instantaneous position $x = 11t^2 - 2t^3$, where t is in seconds and x in metres. Obtain its velocity after 2 s.
If an elevator is accelerating upwards at 3 m/s² while a body of mass 40 kg is on its floor, what is the normal reaction force on the body? (Take g = 9.8 m/s²)
Two bodies A and B are moving on the x-axis with velocities of 5 m/s and 20 m/s, respectively. Find the velocity of A with respect to B?
questions.explanation: Velocity of A relative to B = 5 − 20 = −15 m/s.

questions.text: A particle starts at position $\vec{r}_0 = (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j})$ m with initial velocity $\vec{v}_0 = (4\hat{i} + 6\hat{j})$ m/s and a constant acceleration $\vec{a} = (\hat{i} + 2\hat{j})$ m/s². Find the velocity after 5 seconds.

A particle starts at position $\vec{r}_0 = (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j})$ m with initial velocity $\vec{v}_0 = (4\hat{i} + 6\hat{j})$ m/s and a constant acceleration $\vec{a} = (\hat{i} + 2\hat{j})$ m/s². Find the position after 5 seconds.
A ball is kicked from the ground at 20 m/s at 37° above the horizontal. Take sin 37° = 0.6, cos 37° = 0.8 and g = 10 m/s². Find the time of flight.
questions.explanation: $T = \frac{2v_0\sin\theta}{g} = \frac{2 \times 20 \times 0.6}{10} = 2.4$ s.

questions.text: A ball is kicked from the ground at 20 m/s at 37° above the horizontal. Take sin 37° = 0.6, cos 37° = 0.8 and g = 10 m/s². Find the maximum height.
A ball is kicked from the ground at 20 m/s at 37° above the horizontal. Take sin 37° = 0.6, cos 37° = 0.8 and g = 10 m/s². Find the horizontal range.
questions.explanation: $R = v_0\cos\theta \times T = 16 \times 2.4 = 38.4$ m.

questions.text: A student walks 80 m from the hostel to the library in 60 s, then runs back 40 m towards the hostel in 15 s. What is the total distance travelled?
questions.explanation: Distance adds every part of the path: 80 + 40 = 120 m.

questions.text: A student walks 80 m from the hostel to the library in 60 s, then runs back 40 m towards the hostel in 15 s. What is the total displacement from the hostel?
questions.explanation: The student ends 80 − 40 = 40 m from the hostel, on the library side.

questions.text: A student walks 80 m from the hostel to the library in 60 s, then runs back 40 m towards the hostel in 15 s. What is the average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 120 ÷ 75 = 1.6 m/s.

questions.text: A student walks 80 m from the hostel to the library in 60 s, then runs back 40 m towards the hostel in 15 s. What is the magnitude of the average velocity for the entire journey?
questions.explanation: Average velocity = displacement ÷ total time = 40 ÷ 75 = 0.53 m/s.

held.text: Which of the following mathematical expressions is not a direct statement or consequence explained primarily by Newton's Three Laws of Motion?
held.reason: Two options can be defended (F = Mg and mg = N), so the printed key D can't be confirmed
